title: Parallel classification (cls) vs. autoregressive generation (ar)
question: Holding the prompt and prefix `input_ids` fixed at a single input length L (with `cls` run at `--embedding-mode nope` for a pure `input_ids` match against `ar`, alongside default `token_type_pe`), how does step-by-step prediction via a learned ParallelClassificationHead (predicting o_k and flag_k in parallel) compare in sample efficiency and symbol accuracy against pure-LM next-token prediction via the parameter-free SubspaceLMHead (`ar`)? Caveats: (1) because `x_length = L` is fixed per run, halting is a constant function of output step count in both `ar` and `cls` (variable-length halting is tested in `addition`); (2) both evaluators stop on a premature halt so post-halt steps receive zero credit, whereas at a premature halt on step k itself `cls` still emits `(pred_o[k], FLAG_FINISHED)` on separate heads while emitting `[EOS]` at step k in `ar` occupies the symbol slot; (3) `train.jsonl` logs `loss` in normalised `nats / target` alongside cumulative `tokens_seen` (`2 * L * batch_size` supervised targets/step in `cls` `single_pass` vs `(L + 1) * batch_size` in `ar`); (4) at default `d_model = 512`, `ParallelClassificationHead` adds `+262,656` untied head parameters (`RMSNorm` plus two `512 x 256` projections, including `254` untargeted classes on the 256-way flag head) vs `0` head parameters in `SubspaceLMHead`.
